title: 166. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Factoring a Common Monomial
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Factor a binomial by taking out the greatest common numerical factor.
questions.question: Which expression is the complete factorization of \(6x+9\) by factoring out the greatest common monomial?
questions.explanation:
The greatest common factor of \(6\) and \(9\) is \(3\). Divide each term by \(3\). Therefore:
\[
\begin{aligned}
6x\div 3 &= 2x,\qquad 9\div 3=3\\
6x+9 &= 3(2x+3)
\end{aligned}
\]
questions.hint: Find the greatest common factor of the coefficients, then divide each term by it.

questions.concept: Factoring a Common Monomial with a Variable
questions.learningObjective: Factor a binomial by taking out the greatest common monomial including a variable.
questions.question: Which is the fully factored form of \(8x^2+12x\) using the greatest common monomial?
questions.explanation:
The greatest common factor of \(8x^2\) and \(12x\) is \(4x\). Divide each term by \(4x\). Thus:
\[
\begin{aligned}
8x^2\div 4x &= 2x,\qquad 12x\div 4x=3\\
8x^2+12x &= 4x(2x+3)
\end{aligned}
\]
Option A is not fully factored because \(4x+6\) still has a common factor of \(2\).
questions.hint: Use the greatest common factor of both the coefficients and the variable powers.

questions.concept: Factoring a Common Monomial with Powers
questions.learningObjective: Factor a binomial by taking out the greatest common monomial with variable powers.
questions.question: Factor \(10a^3-15a^2\) by taking out the greatest common monomial.
questions.explanation:
The greatest common factor of \(10a^3\) and \(15a^2\) is \(5a^2\). Divide each term. Therefore:
\[
\begin{aligned}
10a^3\div 5a^2 &= 2a,\qquad 15a^2\div 5a^2=3\\
10a^3-15a^2 &= 5a^2(2a-3)
\end{aligned}
\]
questions.hint: For variable powers, take the lowest power of the common variable.

questions.learningObjective: Factor a binomial by taking out a negative common monomial.
questions.question: Which expression is \(-4x^2-8x\) factored by taking out the common monomial \(-4x\)?
questions.explanation:
Factor out \(-4x\). Divide each term. Thus:
\[
\begin{aligned}
-4x^2\div(-4x) &= x,\qquad -8x\div(-4x)=2\\
-4x^2-8x &= -4x(x+2)
\end{aligned}
\]
questions.hint: When factoring out a negative monomial, divide each term carefully and keep the signs.

questions.concept: Factoring a Common Monomial with Two Variables
questions.learningObjective: Factor a binomial by taking out the greatest common monomial with two variables.
questions.question: Which expression is \(12m^3n-18m^2n^2\) factored by taking out the greatest common monomial?
questions.explanation:
The greatest common factor of \(12m^3n\) and \(18m^2n^2\) is \(6m^2n\). Divide each term. Therefore:
\[
\begin{aligned}
12m^3n\div 6m^2n &= 2m,\qquad 18m^2n^2\div 6m^2n=3n\\
12m^3n-18m^2n^2 &= 6m^2n(2m-3n)
\end{aligned}
\]
questions.hint: For each variable, take the lowest exponent that appears in both terms.

questions.concept: Factoring a Common Monomial from a Trinomial
questions.learningObjective: Factor a trinomial by taking out the common monomial.
questions.question: Factor \(x^3+x^2+x\) by taking out the common monomial.
questions.explanation:
Each term contains a factor of \(x\). Divide each term by \(x\). Thus:
\[
\begin{aligned}
x^3\div x &= x^2,\qquad x^2\div x=x,\qquad x\div x=1\\
x^3+x^2+x &= x(x^2+x+1)
\end{aligned}
\]
Option A is missing the constant term \(1\).
questions.hint: Remember that dividing a term by itself leaves \(1\), not \(0\).

questions.concept: Factoring a Common Numerical Factor from a Trinomial
questions.learningObjective: Factor a trinomial by taking out the greatest common numerical factor.
questions.question: Factor \(2x^2-6x+4\) by taking out the greatest common monomial.
questions.explanation:
The greatest common factor of \(2\), \(6\), and \(4\) is \(2\). Divide each term by \(2\). Therefore:
\[
\begin{aligned}
2x^2\div 2 &= x^2,\qquad -6x\div 2=-3x,\qquad 4\div 2=2\\
2x^2-6x+4 &= 2(x^2-3x+2)
\end{aligned}
\]
questions.hint: Divide every term in the trinomial by the same common factor.

questions.concept: Factoring a Common Monomial from a Multivariable Trinomial
questions.learningObjective: Factor a multivariable trinomial by taking out the greatest common monomial.
questions.question: Factor \(9a^2b-3ab^2+6ab\) by taking out the greatest common monomial.
questions.explanation:
The greatest common factor of \(9a^2b\), \(3ab^2\), and \(6ab\) is \(3ab\). Divide each term. Thus:
\[
\begin{aligned}
9a^2b\div 3ab &= 3a,\qquad -3ab^2\div 3ab=-b,\qquad 6ab\div 3ab=2\\
9a^2b-3ab^2+6ab &= 3ab(3a-b+2)
\end{aligned}
\]
questions.hint: Find the greatest common factor of the coefficients and the lowest power of each variable, then divide every term by it.

questions.concept: Solving an Equation by Factoring a Common Monomial
questions.learningObjective: Solve a quadratic equation by factoring out the common monomial.
questions.question: Solve \(3x^2-6x=0\) by factoring out the common monomial.
questions.explanation:
Factor out the common monomial \(3x\):
\[
3x^2-6x=3x(x-2)=0
\]
Thus, by the zero-product property:
\[
\begin{aligned}
3x=0 \quad &\text{or} \quad x-2=0\\
x=0 \quad &\text{or} \quad x=2
\end{aligned}
\]
questions.hint: After factoring, set each factor equal to zero and solve.

questions.concept: Factoring a Negative Common Monomial from a Trinomial
questions.learningObjective: Factor a trinomial by taking out a negative common monomial.
questions.question: Factor \(-2x^3+4x^2-6x\) by taking out the common monomial \(-2x\).
questions.explanation:
Factor out \(-2x\). Divide each term. Therefore:
\[
\begin{aligned}
-2x^3\div(-2x) &= x^2,\qquad 4x^2\div(-2x)=-2x,\qquad -6x\div(-2x)=3\\
-2x^3+4x^2-6x &= -2x(x^2-2x+3)
\end{aligned}
\]
questions.hint: Divide each term by \(-2x\) and check the signs in the parentheses.
